11 The graph shows how the momentum of a motorcycle changes with time.

What is the resultant force on the motorcycle?
A
500 N
B
5000 N
C
25 000 N
D
50 000 N

hints: Notice the graph is momentum in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ against time in $\text{s}$, rising straight from 0 to 5000 in 10 s.
Recall resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, so $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$ is the gradient of this graph.
Calculate the gradient as $(5000 - 0)/(10 - 0)$ and check the unit reduces to $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given change from the graph: momentum increases from $0$ to $5000 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ in time $10 \text{ s}$, so $\Delta p = 5000 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and $\Delta t = 10 \text{ s}$.
State the governing rule: resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$.
Substitute the values with units: $F = 5000/10$ with units $\text{kg m s}^{-1}/\text{s} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $F = 500 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} = 500 \text{ N}$.
Connect to the options: $500 \text{ N}$ matches the listed value. This is option A.

A.explanation: Rate of change of momentum is $5000/10 = 500$ in units of $\text{N}$, matching the gradient.

B.explanation: 5000 is the final momentum in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, not the rate of change per second.

C.explanation: 25000 would be half the area under the graph, but area of a momentum-time graph is not force.

D.explanation: 50000 is $5000 \times 10$, which multiplies momentum by time instead of dividing change by time.
